info.disambiguation: Noise rock band from San Antonio
info.bio: Los Butthole Surfers son una banda de rock americana fundada en 1981 por Gibby Haynes and Paul Leary en San Antonio, Texas. Son bastante conocidos por su humor negro, y por su sonido que incopora elementos del punk rock, la psicodelia, el heavy metal, el noise rock y la música electrónica. Aclamados por sus shows caóticos y por su particular locura sobre el escenario que no sólo tiene que ver con su imagen sino con el sonido que logra la banda.

scenes.name: Indie, C86 y el giro retro
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: En 1985 la energía se ha disipado: el new pop cae en la decadencia (Live Aid, «una tragedia para el pop»), los singles independientes venden la mitad que en 1980 y «independiente» se convierte en «indie», un género de guitarras sucias, voces pálidas y nostalgia de los sesenta, oposición impotente al mainstream. El futurismo da paso al «rock de coleccionista»: The Jesus and Mary Chain (Psychocandy: Ronettes y Beach Boys con feedback), el sello Creation y Primal Scream, la cassette C86 de NME (The Pastels, Shop Assistants, The Soup Dragons, June Brides) y su culto a la inocencia, que reaparecerá en el riot grrrl. The Smiths y R.E.M., contra los ochenta; Hüsker Dü, Sonic Youth, Butthole Surfers y Dinosaur Jr. redescubren el acid rock; de ahí, Nirvana.

scenes.name: Psicodelia del desierto
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Del desierto de Arizona surge un sonido country-psicodélico: los Meat Puppets tienden un puente entre hardcore y acid-rock y se convierten en herederos de los Grateful Dead con su «cosmic cow-punk» (Up On The Sun); Green On Red, híbrido de garage, new wave y Paisley Underground; Giant Sand de Howe Gelb y su fusión de rock, country y psicodelia. En Texas, el punk hiperpsicodélico demente de los Butthole Surfers (Psychic Powerless), una de las grandes bandas de los ochenta.

podcast.title: Catalyst for Kurt and Courtney's Relationship (1991)
podcast.body: A Butthole Surfers show in Los Angeles on May 29, 1991, served as the occasion where Kurt Cobain and Courtney Love reconnected and solidified their relationship, one month after Nirvana signed their major record deal. This event was a pivotal moment leading to their eventual inseparability. "On May 29th, 1991, one month after Nirvana signed their major deal, Kurt and Courtney hooked up again at a butthole surfer show in Los Angeles."

podcast.title: Lollapalooza 1991 Performer
podcast.body: The Butthole Surfers performed at the first Lollapalooza tour in the summer of 1991, which, by drawing upwards of 20,000 attendees for a lineup of non-mainstream bands, signaled a shift in music tastes towards alternative acts. "Along with founding band Jane's addiction, the line up included Suzy and the band sheets, living color, iced tea and body count, butthole surfers, Rawens band and some weirdo group that was never going to go anywhere called Nine-inch Nails."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Lollapalooza Performance (1991)
podcast.body: The Butthole Surfers participated in the inaugural Lollapalooza tour, which was created to unite various alternative acts and present them in larger venues across America. "It featured Jane's Addiction as the headliners along with up and coming bands like Nine Inch Nails and the Rollins Band along with Ice Tea and Body Counts and the Butthole Surfers and Suzy and the Banshees and more."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Exodus Recovery Center Stay (Spring 1994)
podcast.body: Gibby Haynes was present at the Exodus Recovery Center in Marina del Rey during spring 1994, at the same time Scott Wyland was considering checking into the facility for detox, leading to Wyland's decision not to check in. "There are two major junkies already on the premises and that will not help you kick your habit."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Rehab Companion to Kurt Cobain (1994)
podcast.body: While at the Exodus Recovery Center in Los Angeles in 1994, Gibby Haynes of the Butthole Surfers was a fellow patient and friend to Kurt Cobain. They "hung out and commiserated about their respective situations." "One of the other patients was Gibby Haines of the Butthole Surfers."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Alleged Introduction to Heroin
podcast.body: Gibby Haynes of the Butthole Surfers was reportedly the individual who introduced Scott Wyland to heroin. "The first of those junkies was Gibby Haynes of the Butthole Surfers, the guy who apparently introduced Scott to smack in the first place."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Alleged Introduction to Heroin
podcast.body: Singer Gibby Haynes of the Butthole Surfers allegedly introduced Scott Weiland of Stone Temple Pilots to heroin during a tour in 1993, a story that, regardless of its literal truth, coincided with Weiland's entry into heroin addiction. "The story is that during a tour with the Butthole Surfers, singer Gibby Haynes gave Scott a taste and then, you know, whether the story is true or not doesn't matter because Wyland did get into heroin."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Dog Named Mark Farner
podcast.body: Gibby Haynes, a member of the Butthole Surfers, owned a pit bull named Mark Farner, honoring the guitarist from Grand Funk Railroad. "Gibby Haynes and the Butthole Surfers had a pit bull named Mark Farner after the guy in Grandfell Grille Road."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Tour with Stone Temple Pilots
podcast.body: Stone Temple Pilots opted to tour with the Butthole Surfers in June and July of 1993, turning down an offer to open for Aerosmith due to genre differences. It was during this tour that their singer, Gibby Haynes, allegedly introduced Scott Weiland to heroin. "So they turned that opportunity down in favor of a tour with, wait for it, the Butthole Surfers."

xref.title: Developing Relationship with Courtney Love (1991)
xref.body: After their initial meeting and an exchange of gifts (a heart-shaped box from Courtney), Kurt and Courtney reconnected on May 29, 1991, at a Butthole Surfers show in Los Angeles, one month after Nirvana secured their major record deal. Their "instant attraction" quickly escalated into a physical altercation involving Courtney punching Kurt, followed by wrestling and kicking, and then sharing drugs like Vicodin and high-powered cough syrup, leading to them becoming "pretty much inseparable." "There was instant attraction, especially after Courtney decided to punch Kurt in the stock. That led to some wrestling and kicking, and afterwards they shared some drugs, vikin' in and high powered cough syrup."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Lollapalooza 1991 Founding Band
xref.body: Jane's Addiction was the founding band of the first Lollapalooza tour in the summer of 1991, which featured a diverse lineup of non-mainstream artists and convinced promoters of the commercial viability of such alternative festivals. "Along with founding band Jane's addiction, the line up included Suzy and the band sheets, living color, iced tea and body count, butthole surfers, Rawens band and some weirdo group that was never going to go anywhere called Nine-inch Nails."

xref.title: Heroin Addiction (1993)
xref.body: Scott Weiland's heroin addiction began around 1993, with a story claiming Butthole Surfers' Gibby Haynes introduced him to it during a tour. This addiction created "all kinds of problems for the band." "The story is that during an STP tour with the Butthole surfers, the surfers Gibby Haynes showed Scott how it was done."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Scott Weiland's Drug Addiction (1993 Onwards)
xref.body: Scott Weiland discovered heroin in 1993, allegedly introduced by Gibby Haynes of the Butthole Surfers during a tour. This marked the beginning of his cycle of substance abuse, leading to repeated stints in rehab and jail starting in 1995. "Then in 1993, Wyland discovered that he really liked heroin. The story is that during a tour with the Butthole Surfers, singer Gibby Haynes gave Scott a taste and then, you know, whether the story is true or not doesn't matter because Wyland did get into heroin."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: First Detox Attempt (Spring 1994) – Exodus Recovery Center
xref.body: In spring 1994, Wyland intended to check into the Exodus Recovery Center in Marina del Rey for detox. He was advised against it because two other "major junkies," Gibby Haynes of the Butthole Surfers (who allegedly introduced Wyland to heroin) and Kurt Cobain, were already present. "There are two major junkies already on the premises and that will not help you kick your habit."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Rehab Escape (1994)
xref.body: While at the Exodus Recovery Center, Kurt Cobain befriended fellow patient Gibby Haynes of the Butthole Surfers. On the evening of Good Friday, April 1st, 1994, at 7:25 PM, Cobain told an attendant he was going for a smoke, then scaled a six-foot fence to escape, despite being able to simply walk out under Exodus policy. "Instead, he scaled the six-foot fence and made a break for it, which was unnecessarily dramatic, since under Exodus policy, he could have just walked out the front door."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Drummer for Butthole Surfers
xref.body: Teresa Taylor, also known as Teresa Nervosa, was a member of the Butthole Surfers, a band noted for its challenging and unconventional nature. Her participation demonstrated a toughness required for such a group. "Teresa Taylor, who became known as Teresa Nervosa, was a member of, believe it or not, the Butthole Surfers. You gotta be tough to be in that kind of band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: First Tour and Touring Decisions
xref.body: The first Stone Temple Pilots tour lasted 14 months. After opening for Megadeth, they received an offer to open for Aerosmith. However, the band declined this opportunity, as they did not consider themselves to be in the same genre as Aerosmith during the early 90s alternative music scene. Instead, they opted to tour with the Butthole Surfers in June and July of 1993. "They didn't consider themselves in the same genre as Erosmith."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Introduction to Heroin
xref.body: Scott Weiland was allegedly introduced to heroin by Gibby Haynes, the singer of the Butthole Surfers, during a tour in June and July of 1993. Weiland later claimed his first heroin use occurred in New York on August 4, 1993, following a show at the Roseland Ballroom. "It's alleged that this is when Gibby introduced Scott to heroin."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Member Honored by Gibby Haynes' Dog
xref.body: Mark Farner, a member of Grand Funk Railroad, was the namesake for a pit bull owned by Gibby Haynes of the Butthole Surfers, reflecting the cross-band appreciation. "Gibby Haynes and the Butthole Surfers had a pit bull named Mark Farner after the guy in Grandfell Grille Road."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Ministry/Butthole Surfers Collaboration Recording
xref.body: Al Jourgensen recorded a song with Gibby Haynes of the Butthole Surfers, a process complicated by Haynes being extremely high throughout the entire session. Haynes was only capable of screaming through a megaphone and eventually fell off his stool. Jourgensen dedicated two weeks to meticulously editing all of Haynes's vocal tracks to create usable material for the song. "Gibby was so high the entire time that the only thing he could do is scream stuff through a megaphone and then he fell off his stool."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Other Creative Pursuits and Cocaine Psychosis (1990s)
xref.body: During his period of addiction and depression, John Frusciante focused on painting, attempting to write screenplays, and making demos on a four-track recorder. He also appeared with the band P, which included Johnny Depp and Gibby Haynes of the Butthole Surfers, though nothing substantial came of it. He experienced severe cocaine psychosis from excessive crack and coke use, leading to days-long binges. During one such episode, he called Perry Farrell at 7 AM, asking, "how do you get the snakes out of your eyes?" He also described an elaborate outfit for "waging war against the ghosts" from his roof, covering every part of his body. "My outfit for going up on the roof to wage war against the ghosts. Goggles and my ski mask, with every part of my body covered. No holes, sweatpants tucked into my socks. You couldn't get into me on any level. It made sense at the time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Long Strange Trip of John Frusciante Part 1

xref.title: Pit Bull Named Mark Farner
xref.body: Gibby Haynes, known for his work with the Butthole Surfers, owned a pit bull named Mark Farner. This name was chosen in homage to the musician from the band Grand Funk Railroad. "Gibby Haynes and the Butthole Surfers had a pit bull named Mark Farner after the guy in Grandfell Grille Road."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Producer Role for Butthole Surfers
xref.body: John Paul Jones, widely recognized as the bass player for Led Zeppelin, also took on a producing role for the Butthole Surfers. He produced their 1993 track, "The Annoying Song," from the album "Independent Worms Saloon." "By the way, that song was produced by John Paul Jones, the bass player for Let's Set Plane."
